why: The report silenced, restoring the status quo that made this residue invisible. Worktrees from before the pid naming carry nothing to check a process against, so they are deliberately NOT collected -- but `git status` does not show them and `git worktree prune` does not remove them, so with the report gone the only way to learn they exist is for someone to think to run `git worktree list`. That is how the pair on the development machine went unnoticed across a whole session.
killedBy: staleWorkerWorktrees: collecting a killed run's leftovers (issue #664) NAMES a pre-PID worker worktree instead of silently ignoring it
